tools.name: get_services
tools.description: Returns turva.dev's service catalog and contract terms. The catalog covers the agent-readiness audit, advisory, implementation, the MCP server security test, agent operations and MCP server design. The audit, advisory and implementation have fixed list prices, and the other three are priced on request. One fixed-price implementation add-on, sold only with the audit it follows, is listed under bundled_implementation. Active security testing, an audit add-on priced by quote, is listed under quoted_add_ons. The engagement field holds the working terms of an engagement, including the access the audit and implementation need. Its contract_terms field quotes the engagement terms of the legal page in full: scope, business days, deliverables, payment, cancellation and refunds, delay, continuity, confidentiality, liability, intellectual property and governing law. The sample_report field describes the published sample audit report, a fictional worked example, with its sections and its nine example findings. Use this when a user asks what turva.dev offers or costs, what access an engagement needs, what the contract says, or what a delivered report contains. For the standing principles behind every engagement use get_principles, and for who runs turva.dev, how to reach it and how personal data is handled use get_contact. Read-only: returns static JSON that is compiled into the Worker, so it changes nothing and updates only on deploy.

tools.name: get_agent_readiness
tools.description: Returns how well AI agents can discover and use turva.dev, as scored by one independent public scanner, isitagentready.com: the overall score and level, the category sub-scores, the measurement date and a link to the scanner's start page, where a new check can be run. That link does not open the recorded reading. Use this when a user asks for turva.dev's agent-readiness score or level, or wants to check the readiness claim behind the audit service. It holds no TLS, DNS or email security results, which get_security_evidence returns. When a user asks for evidence in general, call both. Read-only: returns static JSON that is compiled into the Worker, so it changes nothing and updates only on deploy.

tools.name: get_security_evidence
tools.description: Returns the web and email security scan results for turva.dev's own domain from three scans: Hardenize and two Internet.nl tests, one for the site and one for its mail. They cover HTTPS, DNSSEC, RPKI, IPv6 and email authentication, and each has its result, scan date and public report link. Use this when a user asks how turva.dev's own domain is secured or configured. It holds no agent-readiness score, which get_agent_readiness returns. When a user asks for evidence in general, call both. Read-only: returns static JSON that is compiled into the Worker, so it changes nothing and updates only on deploy.

tools.name: get_principles
tools.description: Returns turva.dev's four engagement principles, each with its reason: async-only, least access, each fix checked with a scanner or a direct test, and open and verifiable. Use this when a user asks what turva.dev stands by or why it works the way it does, for example why there are no calls. For the terms of an engagement, its scope, access, dates, payment and prices, use get_services instead, and for how to start use get_contact. Read-only: returns static JSON that is compiled into the Worker, so it changes nothing and updates only on deploy.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: Returns who runs turva.dev, how to reach it and how it handles personal data. The operator field gives the legal form, Business ID, VAT ID and postal address, with the team and the background. Beside it are the email address, the Signal link and the LinkedIn profile, with the correspondence languages, the first-reply time and the first steps to start an audit. The privacy field quotes the privacy sections of the legal page: the controller and lawful bases, server logs, international transfers, email, client material, public-site briefs, outreach records, AI tools, providers, data rights and cookies. Two legal page sections are left out: AI tools in security work, and where the work runs. Use this when a user asks who is behind turva.dev, for its legal details, how to contact it or start an audit, or how it handles personal data. For the services, prices, the access an engagement needs and the contract terms use get_services instead. Read-only: returns static JSON that is compiled into the Worker, so it changes nothing and updates only on deploy.
